subject: general
question: How many beats are there in the Hindustani classical taal named Dadra Taal?
solution:
The correct answer is __**6.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**Dadra Tal:**

__
 
• **Dadra taal, which has six beats,** is quite popular in the lighter types of music.
 
• In India, it is frequently **heard in qawwalis, film songs, bhajans, gazals, and folk music.**
 
• The name is derived from its resemblance to the dadra singing style.
 
• This semiclassical form resembles thumri in certain ways.
 
• The beginning location of the dadra singing style is also where the style gets its name.
 
• Dadra is extremely well-liked for a variety of reasons. One reason is the simplicity of playing in three and six beats; they are fairly symmetrical and present no difficulty.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Different types of taal**

 
• The taal or tal is a repeating rhythm pattern usually played by the tabla.
 
• It usually has between six and sixteen beats.
 
• The beats are grouped into small sections within the pattern. 
 
• There are **mainly six types of tal** in classical music. They are: **Teen taal, dadra taal, keharwa taal, roopak taal, jhap taal, ek taal.**
 
• **Teen taal – 16 Beats**

 Dadra taal – 6 Beats

 Keharwa taal – 8 Beats

 Roopak taal – 7 Beats

 Jhap taal – 10 Beats

 Ek taal – 12 Beats
